tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

schema.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
schema.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

import glob, os, re, sys
import numpy as np, soundfile as sf, subprocess
from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
# Naturalness proxies per clip:
#   te_lp   Whisper's average log-probability decoding it as Telugu (higher = sounds more like fluent Telugu)
#   te_p    Whisper's language-ID confidence that it is Telugu
#   mov     pitch range in semitones (10th..90th pct), jit  mean |frame-to-frame| pitch change in semitones
#   rate    Telugu aksharas per second of speech (scripted clips only)
FF = "ffmpeg"
model = WhisperModel("medium", device="cpu", compute_type="int8")

def load(p):
    raw = subprocess.run([FF, "-v", "error", "-i", p, "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000", "-f", "f32le", "-"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
    return np.frombuffer(raw, np.float32).astype(np.float64)

def f0(x, sr=16000):
    n = int(0.04 * sr); hop = int(0.01 * sr); out = []; thr = np.percentile(np.abs(x), 90) * 0.3
    for i in range(0, len(x) - n, hop):
        f = x[i:i + n] - x[i:i + n].mean()
        if np.abs(f).max() < thr: out.append(np.nan); continue
        ac = np.correlate(f, f, "full")[n - 1:]; lo, hi = sr // 400, sr // 70
        k = lo + np.argmax(ac[lo:hi]); out.append(sr / k if ac[k] > 0.45 * ac[0] else np.nan)
    return np.array(out)

def stats(x, text=None):
    p = f0(x); v = p[~np.isnan(p)]
    st = 12 * np.log2(p / np.nanmedian(p)) if len(v) else p
    d = np.abs(np.diff(st)); d = d[~np.isnan(d)]; d = d[d < 3]          # ignore octave jumps
    mov = 12 * np.log2(np.percentile(v, 90) / np.percentile(v, 10)) if len(v) > 10 else 0
    n = 320; e = np.array([np.sqrt(np.mean(x[i:i+n]**2)) for i in range(0, len(x)-n, n)])
    sp = (e > e.max() * 10 ** (-38/20)).sum() * 0.02
    segs, info = model.transcribe(x.astype(np.float32), language="te", beam_size=5)
    segs = list(segs)
    lp = np.mean([s.avg_logprob for s in segs]) if segs else -9
    _, _, probs = model.detect_language(x.astype(np.float32)) if hasattr(model, "detect_language") else (0, 0, [])
    tep = dict(probs).get("te", 0) if probs else float("nan")
    rate = len(re.sub(r"[^\u0C15-\u0C39\u0C05-\u0C14]", "", text)) / sp if text else float("nan")
    return dict(te_lp=lp, te_p=tep, mov=mov, jit=float(np.mean(d)) if len(d) else 0, rate=rate, f0=float(np.median(v)) if len(v) else 0)

def show(tag, rows):
    keys = ["te_lp", "te_p", "mov", "jit", "rate", "f0"]
    a = {k: np.nanmean([r[k] for r in rows]) for k in keys}
    print(f"{tag:10s} n={len(rows):2d}  " + "  ".join(f"{k} {a[k]:6.2f}" for k in keys), flush=True)

mode = sys.argv[1]
if mode == "refs":
    rows = []
    for p in sorted(glob.glob("C:/tgwork/refs/sep/htdemucs/ref*/vocals.wav")):
        x = load(p)
        for s in range(0, len(x) - 16000 * 6, 16000 * 9):          # 6 s chunks every 9 s
            c = x[s:s + 16000 * 6]
            if np.sqrt(np.mean(c**2)) > 0.01: rows.append(stats(c))
    show("HUMAN refs", rows)
else:
    import json
    lines = json.load(open("C:/tgwork/lines_v2.json", encoding="utf-8"))
    by = {}
    for p in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(sys.argv[2], "*.*"))):
        i, eng = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0].split("_", 1)
        r = stats(load(p), lines[int(i)].get("tts", lines[int(i)]["te"]))
        print(f"  {i} {eng:8s} " + "  ".join(f"{k} {v:6.2f}" for k, v in r.items()), flush=True)
        by.setdefault(eng, []).append(r)
    for eng, rows in by.items(): show(eng, rows)
EOF

# **IndicF5: High-Quality Text-to-Speech for Indian Languages**


We release **IndicF5**, a **near-human polyglot** **Text-to-Speech (TTS)** model trained on **1417 hours** of high-quality speech from **[Rasa](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ai4bharat/Rasa), [IndicTTS](https://www.iitm.ac.in/donlab/indictts/database), [LIMMITS](https://sites.google.com/view/limmits24/), and [IndicVoices-R](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ai4bharat/indicvoices_r)**.  

IndicF5 supports **11 Indian languages**:  
**Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu.**  

🚩**NOTE** 🚩[Indic-Speak](https://huggingface.co/bodhan-ai/indic-speak) is now available. It supports 22 Indian languages and has better text-to-speech capabilities compared to **IndicF5**. We recommend using **Indic-Speak**.

---

## 🚀 Installation
```bash
conda create -n indicf5 python=3.10 -y
conda activate indicf5
pip install git+https://github.com/ai4bharat/IndicF5.git
```


## 🎙 Usage

To generate speech, you need to provide **three inputs**:
1. **Text to synthesize** – The content you want the model to speak.
2. **A reference prompt audio** – An example speech clip that guides the model’s prosody and speaker characteristics.
3. **Text spoken in the reference prompt audio** – The transcript of the reference prompt audio.


```python
from transformers import AutoModel
import numpy as np
import soundfile as sf

# Load IndicF5 from Hugging Face
repo_id = "ai4bharat/IndicF5"
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(repo_id, trust_remote_code=True)

# Generate speech
audio = model(
    "नमस्ते! संगीत की तरह जीवन भी खूबसूरत होता है, बस इसे सही ताल में जीना आना चाहिए.",
    ref_audio_path="prompts/PAN_F_HAPPY_00001.wav",
    ref_text="ਭਹੰਪੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਮਾਰਕਾਂ ਦੇ ਭਵਨ ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਕਲਾ ਦੇ ਵੇਰਵੇ ਗੁੰਝਲਦਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਹੈਰਾਨ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਹਨ, ਜੋ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਖੁਸ਼ ਕਰਦੇ  ਹਨ।"
)

# Normalize and save output
if audio.dtype == np.int16:
    audio = audio.astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
sf.write("namaste.wav", np.array(audio, dtype=np.float32), samplerate=24000)
print("Audio saved succesfully.")
```

What is Indic-Speak?

Indic-Speak turns written text into natural-sounding speech across 22 Indian languages and English. It is a general-purpose voice engine — you can use it for an app, a helpline, an audiobook, or anything else that needs to talk. But it was built with one audience in mind first: students. Most of the effort went into two problems that matter enormously in Indian education and that almost every other voice system handles badly — reading STEM content correctly, and reading sentences that mix an Indian language with English. The result is a voice that sounds like a teacher explaining something, rather than a machine reading a list. That difference is subtle in a single sentence and very obvious across a ten-minute lesson. ---

Key Features

Built for students first

- **STEM content that is actually correct.** Equations, units, fractions, exponents, and chemical formulae are read the way a teacher reads them in a classroom. - **Code-mixed speech, read naturally.** Indian teaching is rarely in one language; Indic-Speak reads mixed sentences in one continuous voice. - **Paced for comprehension.** The default delivery is explanatory and unhurried rather than brisk and announcement-like.

Capabilities and use cases

Indic-Speak provides several voices per production language, spanning gender, age, and region. English terms, acronyms, and numerals sitting inside an Indic sentence are read in the surrounding voice and accent. import sys
import os

current_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.append(current_dir)

from transformers import PreTrainedModel, PretrainedConfig, AutoConfig
import torch
import numpy as np
from f5_tts.infer.utils_infer import (
    infer_process,
    load_model,
    load_vocoder,
    preprocess_ref_audio_text,
)
from f5_tts.model import DiT
import soundfile as sf
import io
from pydub import AudioSegment, silence
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from safetensors.torch import load_file
import os

class INF5Config(PretrainedConfig):
    model_type = "inf5"

    def __init__(self, ckpt_path: str = "checkpoints/model_best.pt", vocab_path: str = "checkpoints/vocab.txt", 
                 speed: float = 1.0, remove_sil: bool = True, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.ckpt_path = ckpt_path
        self.vocab_path = vocab_path
        self.speed = speed
        self.remove_sil = remove_sil

class INF5Model(PreTrainedModel):
    config_class = INF5Config

    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__(config)
        device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

        # Load vocoder
        self.vocoder = torch.compile(load_vocoder(vocoder_name="vocos", is_local=False, device=device))

        # Download and load model weights
        # safetensors_path = hf_hub_download(config.name_or_path, filename="model.safetensors")
        # print(f"Loading model weights from {safetensors_path} (safetensors)...")
        # state_dict = load_file(safetensors_path, device=str(device))

        # Download vocab.txt from HF Hub
        vocab_path = hf_hub_download(config.name_or_path, filename="checkpoints/vocab.txt")

        self.ema_model = torch.compile(load_model(
                DiT,
                dict(dim=1024, depth=22, heads=16, ff_mult=2, text_dim=512, conv_layers=4),
                mel_spec_type="vocos",
                vocab_file=vocab_path,
                device=device
            )
        )

        # # Load state dict into model
        # self.ema_model.load_state_dict(state_dict, strict=False)

    
    def forward(self, text: str, ref_audio_path: str, ref_text: str):
        """
        Generate speech given a reference audio & text input.
        
        Args:
            text (str): The text to be synthesized.
            ref_audio_path (str): Path to the reference audio file.
            ref_text (str): The reference text.

        Returns:
            np.array: Generated waveform.
        """

        if not os.path.exists(ref_audio_path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Reference audio file {ref_audio_path} not found.")

        # Load reference audio & text
        ref_audio, ref_text = preprocess_ref_audio_text(ref_audio_path, ref_text)

        
        self.ema_model.to(self.device)
        self.vocoder.to(self.device)
        
        # Perform inference
        audio, final_sample_rate, _ = infer_process(
            ref_audio,
            ref_text,
            text,
            self.ema_model,
            self.vocoder,
            mel_spec_type="vocos",
            speed=self.config.speed,
            device=self.device,
        )

        # Convert to pydub format and remove silence if needed
        buffer = io.BytesIO()
        sf.write(buffer, audio, samplerate=24000, format="WAV")
        buffer.seek(0)
        audio_segment = AudioSegment.from_file(buffer, format="wav")

        if self.config.remove_sil:
            non_silent_segs = silence.split_on_silence(
                audio_segment,
                min_silence_len=1000,
                silence_thresh=-50,
                keep_silence=500,
                seek_step=10,
            )
            non_silent_wave = sum(non_silent_segs, AudioSegment.silent(duration=0))
            audio_segment = non_silent_wave

        # Normalize loudness
        target_dBFS = -20.0
        change_in_dBFS = target_dBFS - audio_segment.dBFS
        audio_segment = audio_segment.apply_gain(change_in_dBFS)

        return np.array(audio_segment.get_array_of_samples())



if __name__ == '__main__':
    model = INF5Model(INF5Config(ckpt_path="checkpoints/model_best.pt", vocab_path="checkpoints/vocab.txt"))
    model.save_pretrained("INF5")
    model.config.save_pretrained("INF5")

    import numpy as np
    import soundfile as sf
    from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoModel
    
    AutoConfig.register("inf5", INF5Config)
    AutoModel.register(INF5Config, INF5Model)

    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("INF5")
    audio = model("नमस्ते! संगीत की तरह जीवन भी खूबसूरत होता है, बस इसे सही ताल में जीना आना चाहिए.", 
                  ref_audio_path="prompts/PAN_F_HAPPY_00001.wav",
                  ref_text="भਹੰਪੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਮਾਰਕਾਂ ਦੇ ਭਵਨ ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਕਲਾ ਦੇ ਵੇਰਵੇ ਗੁੰਝਲਦਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਹੈਰਾਨ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਹਨ, ਜੋ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਖੁਸ਼ ਕਰਦੇ  ਹਨ।")
    
    if audio.dtype == np.int16:
        audio = audio.astype(np.float32) / 32768.0  
    sf.write("samples/namaste.wav", np.array(audio, dtype=np.float32), samplerate=24000)

    from huggingface_hub import HfApi

    repo_id = "svp19/INF5"  # Change to your HF repo

    # Upload model directory to HF
    api = HfApi()
    api.upload_folder(
        folder_path="INF5",
        repo_id=repo_id,
        repo_type="model"
    )
    print(f"Model pushed to https://huggingface.co/{repo_id} 🚀")

    print("Verify Upload")
    from transformers import AutoModel
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(repo_id)
    print("Success")

import json, os, sys, time
import numpy as np, soundfile as sf, torch
from safetensors.torch import load_file
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from f5_tts.model import CFM, DiT
from f5_tts.model.utils import get_tokenizer
from f5_tts.infer.utils_infer import infer_process, load_vocoder, preprocess_ref_audio_text

# IndicF5 weights loaded into the PyPI F5-TTS architecture (same config as the model card's wrapper).
# usage: f5_gen.py lines.json outdir idx[,idx..]|all prompts.json [seeds] [speed]
lines_json, outdir, which, prompts_json = sys.argv[1:5]
SEEDS = [int(s) for s in (sys.argv[5] if len(sys.argv) > 5 else "1").split(",")]
SPEED = float(sys.argv[6]) if len(sys.argv) > 6 else 1.0
REPO = "ai4bharat/IndicF5"
torch.set_num_threads(os.cpu_count())

sd = load_file(hf_hub_download(REPO, "model.safetensors"))
vocab, vsize = get_tokenizer(hf_hub_download(REPO, "checkpoints/vocab.txt"), "custom")
model = CFM(transformer=DiT(dim=1024, depth=22, heads=16, ff_mult=2, text_dim=512, conv_layers=4,
                            text_num_embeds=vsize, mel_dim=100),
            mel_spec_kwargs=dict(n_fft=1024, hop_length=256, win_length=1024, n_mel_channels=100,
                                 target_sample_rate=24000, mel_spec_type="vocos"),
            odeint_kwargs=dict(method="euler"), vocab_char_map=vocab)
p = "ema_model._orig_mod."
missing, unexpected = model.load_state_dict({k[len(p):]: v for k, v in sd.items() if k.startswith(p)}, strict=False)
assert not [m for m in missing if "mel_spec" not in m], missing
model.eval()
vocoder = load_vocoder("vocos", is_local=False, device="cpu")
vp = "vocoder._orig_mod."
vocoder.load_state_dict({k[len(vp):]: v for k, v in sd.items() if k.startswith(vp)}, strict=False)

lines = json.load(open(lines_json, encoding="utf-8"))
prompts = json.load(open(prompts_json, encoding="utf-8"))   # {key: {"wav":..., "text":...}}
idx = range(len(lines)) if which == "all" else [int(a) for a in which.split(",")]
os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
cache = {}
for i in idx:
    ln = lines[i]
    key = ln["spk"] + ("_" + ln["style"] if ln["spk"] == "dad" else "")
    pr = prompts.get(key) or prompts[ln["spk"]] if ln["spk"] in prompts or key in prompts else None
    if pr is None:
        print(f"{i:02d} no prompt for {key}, skipped", flush=True); continue
    if key not in cache:
        cache[key] = preprocess_ref_audio_text(pr["wav"], pr["text"])
    ref_audio, ref_text = cache[key]
    for s in SEEDS:
        path = os.path.join(outdir, f"{i:02d}_f{s}.wav")
        if os.path.exists(path): continue
        torch.manual_seed(s * 1000 + i)
        t0 = time.time()
        wav, sr, _ = infer_process(ref_audio, ref_text, ln.get("tts", ln["te"]), model, vocoder,
                                   mel_spec_type="vocos", speed=SPEED, nfe_step=32, cfg_strength=2.0,
                                   sway_sampling_coef=-1.0, device="cpu", show_info=lambda *a: None)
        sf.write(path, wav, sr)
        print(f"{i:02d} f{s} {key} {len(wav)/sr:.2f}s ({time.time()-t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
print("done")

from safetensors.torch import load_file
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from f5_tts.model import CFM, DiT
from f5_tts.model.utils import get_tokenizer
from f5_tts.infer.utils_infer import infer_process, load_vocoder, preprocess_ref_audio_text

# IndicF5 weights loaded into the PyPI F5-TTS architecture (same config as the model card's wrapper).
# usage: f5_gen.py lines.json outdir idx[,idx..]|all prompts.json [seeds] [speed]
lines_json, outdir, which, prompts_json = sys.argv[1:5]
SEEDS = [int(s) for s in (sys.argv[5] if len(sys.argv) > 5 else "1").split(",")]
SPEED = float(sys.argv[6]) if len(sys.argv) > 6 else 1.0
REPO = "ai4bharat/IndicF5"
torch.set_num_threads(os.cpu_count())

sd = load_file(hf_hub_download(REPO, "model.safetensors"))
vocab, vsize = get_tokenizer(hf_hub_download(REPO, "checkpoints/vocab.txt"), "custom")
model = CFM(transformer=DiT(dim=1024, depth=22, heads=16, ff_mult=2, text_dim=512, conv_layers=4,
                            text_num_embeds=vsize, mel_dim=100),
            mel_spec_kwargs=dict(n_fft=1024, hop_length=256, win_length=1024, n_mel_channels=100,
                                 target_sample_rate=24000, mel_spec_type="vocos"),
            odeint_kwargs=dict(method="euler"), vocab_char_map=vocab)
p = "ema_model._orig_mod."
missing, unexpected = model.load_state_dict({k[len(p):]: v for k, v in sd.items() if k.startswith(p)}, strict=False)
assert not [m for m in missing if "mel_spec" not in m], missing
model.eval()
vocoder = load_vocoder("vocos", is_local=False, device="cpu")
vp = "vocoder._orig_mod."
vocoder.load_state_dict({k[len(vp):]: v for k, v in sd.items() if k.startswith(vp)}, strict=False)

lines = json.load(open(lines_json, encoding="utf-8"))
prompts = json.load(open(prompts_json, encoding="utf-8"))   # {key: {"wav":..., "text":...}}
idx = range(len(lines)) if which == "all" else [int(a) for a in which.split(",")]
os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
cache = {}
for i in idx:
    ln = lines[i]
    key = ln["spk"] + ("_" + ln["style"] if ln["spk"] == "dad" else "")
    pr = prompts.get(key) or prompts[ln["spk"]] if ln["spk"] in prompts or key in prompts else None
    if pr is None:
        print(f"{i:02d} no prompt for {key}, skipped", flush=True); continue
    if key not in cache:
        cache[key] = preprocess_ref_audio_text(pr["wav"], pr["text"])
    ref_audio, ref_text = cache[key]
    for s in SEEDS:
        path = os.path.join(outdir, f"{i:02d}_f{s}.wav")
        if os.path.exists(path): continue
        torch.manual_seed(s * 1000 + i)
        t0 = time.time()
        wav, sr, _ = infer_process(ref_audio, ref_text, ln.get("tts", ln["te"]), model, vocoder,
                                   mel_spec_type="vocos", speed=SPEED, nfe_step=32, cfg_strength=2.0,
                                   sway_sampling_coef=-1.0, device="cpu", show_info=lambda *a: None)
        sf.write(path, wav, sr)
        print(f"{i:02d} f{s} {key} {len(wav)/sr:.2f}s ({time.time()-t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
print("done")
EOF

def infer_batch_process(
    ref_audio,
    ref_text,
    gen_text_batches,
    model_obj,
    vocoder,
    mel_spec_type="vocos",
    progress=tqdm,
    target_rms=0.1,
    cross_fade_duration=0.15,
    nfe_step=32,
    cfg_strength=2.0,
    sway_sampling_coef=-1,
    speed=1,
    fix_duration=None,
    device=None,
    streaming=False,
    chunk_size=2048,
):
    audio, sr = ref_audio
    if audio.shape[0] > 1:
        audio = torch.mean(audio, dim=0, keepdim=True)

    rms = torch.sqrt(torch.mean(torch.square(audio)))
    if rms < target_rms:
        audio = audio * target_rms / rms
    if sr != target_sample_rate:
        resampler = torchaudio.transforms.Resample(sr, target_sample_rate)
        audio = resampler(audio)
    audio = audio.to(device)

    generated_waves = []
    spectrograms = []

    if len(ref_text[-1].encode("utf-8")) == 1:
        ref_text = ref_text + " "

    def process_batch(gen_text):
        local_speed = speed
        if len(gen_text.encode("utf-8")) < 10:
            local_speed = 0.3

        # Prepare the text
        text_list = [ref_text + gen_text]
        final_text_list = convert_char_to_pinyin(text_list)

        ref_audio_len = audio.shape[-1] // hop_length
        if fix_duration is not None:
            duration = int(fix_duration * target_sample_rate / hop_length)
        else:
            # Calculate duration
            ref_text_len = len(ref_text.encode("utf-8"))
            gen_text_len = len(gen_text.encode("utf-8"))
            duration = ref_audio_len + int(ref_audio_len / ref_text_len * gen_text_len / local_speed)

        # inference
        with torch.inference_mode():
            generated, _ = model_obj.sample(
                cond=audio,
                text=final_text_list,
                duration=duration,
                steps=nfe_step,
                cfg_strength=cfg_strength,
                sway_sampling_coef=sway_sampling_coef,
            )

            generated = generated.to(torch.float32)
            generated = generated[:, ref_audio_len:, :]
            generated_mel_spec = generated.permute(0, 2, 1)
            if mel_spec_type == "vocos":
                generated_wave = vocoder.decode(generated_mel_spec)
            elif mel_spec_type == "bigvgan":
                generated_wave = vocoder(generated_mel_spec)
            if rms < target_rms:
                generated_wave = generated_wave * rms / target_rms

            # wav -> numpy
            generated_wave = generated_wave.squeeze().cpu().numpy()

            if streaming:
                for j in range(0, len(generated_wave), chunk_size):
                    yield generated_wave[j : j + chunk_size], target_sample_rate
            else:
                yield generated_wave, generated_mel_spec[0].cpu().numpy()

    if streaming:
        for gen_text in progress.tqdm(gen_text_batches) if progress is not None else gen_text_batches:
            for chunk in process_batch(gen_text):
                yield chunk
    else:
        with ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
            futures = [executor.submit(process_batch, gen_text) for gen_text in gen_text_batches]
            for future in progress.tqdm(futures) if progress is not None else futures:
                result = future.result()
                if result:
                    generated_wave, generated_mel_spec = next(result)
                    generated_waves.append(generated_wave)
                    spectrograms.append(generated_mel_spec)

                # Simply concatenate
                final_wave = np.concatenate(generated_waves)

                    cross_fade_samples = min(cross_fade_samples, len(prev_wave), len(next_wave))

import difflib, glob, json, os, re, sys
from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
# Pronunciation accuracy per engine: Whisper (Devanagari read-back) vs the script, as in pick_takes.py.
lines = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
model = WhisperModel("medium", device="cpu", compute_type="int8")
deva = lambda t: "".join(chr(ord(c) - 0x300) if 0x0C00 <= ord(c) <= 0x0C7F else c for c in t)
norm = lambda s: re.sub(r"[^ऀ-ॿ]", "", s).replace("़", "")
by = {}
for p in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(sys.argv[2], "*.*"))):
    i, eng = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0].split("_", 1)
    want = norm(deva(lines[int(i)].get("tts", lines[int(i)]["te"])))
    heard = " ".join(s.text for s in model.transcribe(p, language="hi", beam_size=5)[0])
    sim = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, want, norm(heard)).ratio()
    by.setdefault(eng, []).append(sim)
    print(f"{i} {eng:8s} {sim:.2f}  {heard.strip()}", flush=True)
for eng, v in by.items(): print(f"{eng:8s} mean read-back {sum(v)/len(v):.2f}  min {min(v):.2f}")
EOF

content.text:
V3 isn't ready yet. The new voices are still generating in the background: 11 of 50 lines are done, about an hour to go.

**Engine choice: IndicF5**
- I tested three Telugu engines on the same 8 narrator lines: Indic Parler-TTS (V2's), Microsoft's Telugu voice and AI4Bharat's IndicF5.
- All three pronounce about equally accurately on my automated check. Microsoft's voice sounded flatter: in my measurements its pitch varied less, like a news reader.
- IndicF5 was trained on hundreds of hours of real Telugu speakers, so its rhythm and word connections are the most human of the three. It's also MIT-licensed, so it's safe to monetize.
- To keep your characters, each one's IndicF5 voice is based on a short sample of that character's V2 voice, not any real person's voice.
- It runs a little slower than its default so it doesn't sound rushed. Lines that are long for their scene are spoken slightly faster by the model itself, not stretched afterwards, and never past 1.1×.

**Script:** 26 lines are reworded into everyday spoken Telugu with the same meaning. For example, "మెషిన్" replaces the bookish "యంత్రం", the heart "దడదడలాడిపోయింది", and "అసలు శిక్ష" replaces "అసలు మూల్యం". Subtitles will follow the new wording.

**Next, without needing anything from you:**
1. Check every line for pronunciation, missing or repeated words and odd pauses.
2. Regenerate only the weak lines.
3. Sync, mix with the same music balance as V2, add subtitles and render.
4. Run the full QA and save `Truth_Machine_Telugu_V3_FINAL.mp4` in Downloads, leaving V1 and V2 untouched.

I can't listen to audio myself, so I'll also include a short V2-vs-V3 comparison clip.

To get IndicF5 running, I had to work around a few library files that Windows Smart App Control blocked. I didn't change any security settings: I skipped those parts because only training and plotting use them, not voice generation.

import glob, json, os, subprocess, sys
import numpy as np
# Text-free delivery checks (no transcription):
#   syl/s  syllable rate from loudness peaks (comparable with the human reference narrators)
#   mov    pitch range in semitones, pauses/s, tail = stray sound after a >0.35 s gap at the end
#   clicks sample jumps far above the local level, noisy = loud frames that are noise-like (garble/hiss)
SR = 16000
def load(p):
    raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", p, "-ac", "1", "-ar", str(SR), "-f", "f32le", "-"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
    return np.frombuffer(raw, np.float32).astype(np.float64)

def env(x, hop=160):
    n = len(x) // hop
    return np.sqrt((x[:n*hop].reshape(n, hop) ** 2).mean(1) + 1e-12)

def syllables(e):
    # smoothed envelope peaks, >= 90 ms apart, rising >= 3 dB above the preceding dip
    k = np.hanning(7); s = np.convolve(e, k / k.sum(), "same"); db = 20 * np.log10(s)
    thr = db.max() - 30; peaks, last, dip = 0, -99, db[0]
    for i in range(1, len(db) - 1):
        dip = min(dip, db[i])
        if db[i] > db[i-1] and db[i] >= db[i+1] and db[i] > thr and db[i] - dip > 3 and i - last >= 9:
            peaks += 1; last = i; dip = db[i]
    return peaks

def f0mov(x):
    n = 640; out = []; thr = np.percentile(np.abs(x), 90) * 0.3
    for i in range(0, len(x) - n, 320):
        f = x[i:i+n] - x[i:i+n].mean()
        if np.abs(f).max() < thr: continue
        ac = np.correlate(f, f, "full")[n-1:]; k = 40 + np.argmax(ac[40:228])
        if ac[k] > 0.45 * ac[0]: out.append(SR / k)
    return 12 * np.log2(np.percentile(out, 90) / np.percentile(out, 10)) if len(out) > 10 else 0.0

def check(x):
    e = env(x); db = 20 * np.log10(e); loud = db > db.max() - 35
    idx = np.where(loud)[0]
    if len(idx) < 5: return None
    seg = loud[idx[0]:idx[-1]+1]; speech = seg.sum() * 0.01
    runs, r = [], 0
    for v in seg:
        if v: (runs.append(r) if r else None); r = 0
        else: r += 1

        fix = max(fix, 0.2 * chars, 0.8)        # very short words came out clipped"""
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, "        fix = max(fix, 0.8)                     # very short words came out clipped")
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
import json, soundfile as sf, numpy as np
L = json.load(open("C:/tgwork/lines_v3.json", encoding="utf-8")); P = json.load(open("C:/tgwork/v3/prompts/prompts.json", encoding="utf-8"))
def speech_len(x, sr):
    n = int(0.02*sr); e = np.array([np.sqrt(np.mean(x[i:i+n]**2)) for i in range(0, len(x)-n, n)])
    idx = np.where(e > e.max()*10**(-42/20))[0]; return (idx[-1]-idx[0]+2)*0.02
todo = []
for i, ln in enumerate(L):
    key = ln["spk"] + ("_" + ln["style"] if ln["spk"] == "dad" else "")
    pr = P.get(key) or P.get(ln["spk"]) or P["dad_calm"]

    text = ln.get("tts", ln["te"])
    nat = ref_len / len((pr["text"] + " ").encode()) * len(text.encode()) * 256 / 24000
    fix = max(min(nat / 0.78, max(ln["slot"] * 0.92, nat / 1.1)), 0.8)

print(",".join(map(str, todo)), len(todo))
EOF

import glob, subprocess, sys
import numpy as np, soundfile as sf
sys.path.insert(0, "C:/tgwork/scripts")
import prosody as P
# Per reference: delivery (syllable rate, pitch range, pauses), F0, voice-over-music, music swell in gaps, loudness.
def vom(voc, bed, sr):
    k = min(len(bed), len(voc)); n = int(sr * 0.05); f = k // n
    vr = np.sqrt((voc[:f*n].reshape(f, n)**2).mean(1) + 1e-12); mr = np.sqrt((bed[:f*n].reshape(f, n)**2).mean(1) + 1e-12)
    sp = vr > np.percentile(vr, 95) * 0.15
    return 20*np.log10(vr[sp].mean()/mr[sp].mean()), 20*np.log10(mr[~sp].mean()/mr[sp].mean()), sp.mean()
def f0med(x):
    n = 640; out = []; thr = np.percentile(np.abs(x), 90) * 0.3
    for i in range(0, len(x) - n, 640):
        f = x[i:i+n] - x[i:i+n].mean()
        if np.abs(f).max() < thr: continue
        ac = np.correlate(f, f, "full")[n-1:]; k = 40 + np.argmax(ac[40:228])
        if ac[k] > 0.45 * ac[0]: out.append(P.SR / k)
    return float(np.median(out)) if out else 0
for d in sorted(glob.glob(sys.argv[1] + "/*/")):
    voc, sr = sf.read(d + "vocals.wav"); bed, _ = sf.read(d + "no_vocals.wav")
    voc = voc.mean(1); bed = bed.mean(1)
    v, sw, frac = vom(voc, bed, sr)
    x = P.load(d + "vocals.wav"); rows = [r for s in range(0, len(x) - P.SR*8, P.SR*4) if np.sqrt(np.mean(x[s:s+P.SR*8]**2)) > 0.01 for r in [P.check(x[s:s+P.SR*8])] if r]
    src = d.rstrip("/\\").split("\\")[-1].split("/")[-1]
    lufs = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-nostats", "-i", f"C:/tgwork/reels/refs/audio/{src}.wav", "-af", "ebur128", "-f", "null", "-"], capture_output=True, text=True).stderr
    I = lufs[lufs.rfind("I:"):].split()[1]
    print(f"{src}: syl {np.median([r['syl'] for r in rows]):.2f}/s  pitch range {np.median([r['mov'] for r in rows]):.1f} st  pauses {np.median([r['pauses'] for r in rows]):.2f}/s  "
          f"F0 {f0med(x):.0f} Hz  voice-over-music {v:.1f} dB  gap swell {sw:+.1f} dB  speech {frac*100:.0f}%  loudness {I} LUFS")
EOF

import sys, torch, soundfile as sf
from parler_tts import ParlerTTSForConditionalGeneration
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
# One synthetic Parler voice sample to use as an IndicF5 character prompt (no real person's voice).
desc, text, out, seed = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], int(sys.argv[4])
M = "ai4bharat/indic-parler-tts"
model = ParlerTTSForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(M).eval(); tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(M)
dt = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model.config.text_encoder._name_or_path)

EOF

# Background = music/SFX stem + vocals stem with every English speech window muted.
# Keeping the vocals stem outside speech preserves crowd laughter, boos and gasps.

import json, sys

# Telugu ASS + SRT subtitles for a reel, laid out from the preset (sized to the video, centred on
# the original caption strip). usage: reel_make_ass.py timed.json preset.json W H caption_y out.ass out.srt
timed_json, preset_json, W, H, Y, out_ass, out_srt = sys.argv[1:8]
W, H, Y = int(W), int(H), int(Y)
lines = json.load(open(timed_json, encoding="utf-8"))
sub = json.load(open(preset_json, encoding="utf-8"))["subtitles"]
FS = round(sub["font_px_per_1000w"] * W / 1000)

HEADER = f"""[Script Info]
ScriptType: v4.00+
PlayResX: {W}
PlayResY: {H}
WrapStyle: 2
ScaledBorderAndShadow: yes

[V4+ Styles]
Format: Name, Fontname, Fontsize, PrimaryColour, SecondaryColour, OutlineColour, BackColour, Bold, Italic, Underline, StrikeOut, ScaleX, ScaleY, Spacing, Angle, BorderStyle, Outline, Shadow, Alignment, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Encoding
Style: TE,{sub['font']},{FS},&H00FFFFFF,&H00FFFFFF,&H00101010,&H90000000,1,0,0,0,100,100,0,0,1,{FS*0.077:.1f},{FS*0.039:.1f},5,{W//16},{W//16},0,1

[Events]
Format: Layer, Start, End, Style, Name, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Effect, Text
"""

def ts(t, srt=False):
    t = max(0.0, t); h, r = divmod(t, 3600); m, s = divmod(r, 60)
    return f"{int(h):02d}:{int(m):02d}:{int(s):02d},{int(round((s % 1) * 1000)) % 1000:03d}" if srt else f"{int(h)}:{int(m):02d}:{s:05.2f}"

def wrap(text, limit):
    # balance into at most two lines, breaking only at spaces
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return [text]
    words = text.split(" ")
    return min(([" ".join(words[:i]), " ".join(words[i:])] for i in range(1, len(words))),
               key=lambda ab: abs(len(ab[0]) - len(ab[1])))

with open(out_ass, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fa, open(out_srt, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fs:
    fa.write(HEADER)
    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
        # hold each subtitle a moment after the voice ends, but never into the next line
        end = ln["end"] + 0.3
        if i + 1 < len(lines):
            end = min(end, lines[i + 1]["start"] - 0.02)
        rows = wrap(ln["te"], sub["wrap_chars"])
        fa.write(f"Dialogue: 0,{ts(ln['start'])},{ts(end)},TE,,0,0,0,,{{\pos({W // 2},{Y})}}{chr(92) + 'N'.join(rows) if False else (chr(92) + 'N').join(rows)}\n")
        fs.write(f"{i + 1}\n{ts(ln['start'], True)} --> {ts(end, True)}\n" + "\n".join(rows) + "\n\n")
print("wrote", out_ass, "and", out_srt, len(lines), "events, font", FS)

import json, subprocess, sys

# Final render: cover band (whenever an English caption or Telugu subtitle is on screen),
# Telugu subtitles, background + Telugu voice mix. H.264/AAC MP4 at source resolution.
video, timed_json, ass, background, voice, out = sys.argv[1:7]
timed = json.load(open(timed_json, encoding="utf-8"))

windows = []
for ln in timed:
    windows.append((ln["en_start"] - 0.3, ln["en_end"] + 0.3))
    windows.append((ln["start"] - 0.1, ln["end"] + 0.3))
windows.sort()
merged = []
for a, b in windows:
    if merged and a <= merged[-1][1] + 0.4:
        merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], b)
    else:
        merged.append([max(0, a), b])
enable = "+".join(f"between(t,{a:.2f},{b:.2f})" for a, b in merged)

def probe(path):
    return float(subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", path],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip())

# Hold the last frame (and pad the background) only if the Telugu voice outlasts the picture.
extra = max(0.0, probe(voice) - probe(video))
hold = f",tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration={extra:.2f}" if extra > 0.01 else ""
bgpad = f"apad=pad_dur={extra:.2f}," if extra > 0.01 else ""
print(f"holding last frame for {extra:.2f}s" if hold else "no frame hold needed")

# cover band geometry comes from the caption strip found for this video: COVER="y0,height"
import os
y0, bh = (int(v) for v in os.environ["COVER"].split(","))
w = int(subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "v:0", "-show_entries", "stream=width", "-of", "csv=p=0", video],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip())
template = (f"split[a][b];[b]crop={w}:{bh}:0:{y0},boxblur=16:3,colorlevels=romax=0.55:gomax=0.55:bomax=0.55,format=yuva420p,"
            f"geq=lum='p(X,Y)':cb='p(X,Y)':cr='p(X,Y)':a='255*min(1,min(Y,{bh - 1}-Y)/20)'[band];"
            f"[a][band]overlay=0:{y0}:enable='ENABLE',subtitles=SUBS:fontsdir=C\:/Windows/Fonts")
vf = template.replace("ENABLE", enable).replace("SUBS", ass.replace("\\", "/").replace(":", "\\\\:"))
filt = (f"[0:v]{vf}{hold}[v];[1:a]{bgpad}anull[bg];"
        f"[bg][2:a]amix=inputs=2:duration=longest:normalize=0:weights='0.8 0.8',"
        f"loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1.5:LRA=11,aresample=44100[a]")
cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-stats", "-y", "-i", video, "-i", background, "-i", voice,
       "-filter_complex", filt, "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]",
       "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "slow", "-crf", "16", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-profile:v", "high",
       "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-ar", "44100", "-movflags", "+faststart", out]
print(len(merged), "cover windows")
subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

    print(f"line {i:02d} {ln['start']:6.2f}s lang={lang} ({prob:.2f}) en={en:.2f}{flag}")

V3 is finished, and so is the Telugu pilot for the reels project. I've stopped there as your prompt asks: the other 39 videos haven't been touched.

## Truth Machine V3
- **Final video:** `Downloads\Truth_Machine_Telugu_V3_FINAL.mp4` (attached).
- **Comparison clip:** `Downloads\Truth_Machine_V2_vs_V3_comparison.mp4` (attached). It plays three scenes, each as V2 then V3, so you can judge the fluency by ear. I can't listen to audio, so your ear is the real test.
- **V1 and V2:** unchanged; their checksums still match.

**What changed:**
- **Voice engine:** every voice is now IndicF5, trained on real Telugu speakers. Each character keeps their V2 voice as the starting point.
- **Wording:** 26 lines now use everyday spoken Telugu ("మెషిన్", "దడదడలాడిపోయింది", "ప్రామిస్‌లు").
- **Meaning check:** I checked every rewritten line against the English. Four needed fixing, and "London" is back in line 24.
- **Regenerated takes:** 16 lines got new takes, because they had a clipped word, a stutter, changed wording, or room in the scene for a calmer pace.

**Checks on the exported file:**
- **Format:** H.264/AAC, 576×1024.
- **Audio levels:** −14.4 LUFS, zero clipped samples.
- **Language:** no English in the background; every flagged "English" word is romanized Telugu inside a Telugu line.
- **Subtitles:** all 50 match the spoken V3 wording.
- **English captions:** all 305 caption samples are covered.

**Not fully resolved:**
- **Pace:** V3 speaks at about 6.7 syllables per second, a little faster than V2's 6.4. That's within your new references' range (5.3–7.0), but faster than the earlier 7 references (about 5.5). The English scene timings leave little room to slow down.
- **Late narration:** lines 24–27 run up to 1.3 seconds late, because "London" was restored. They play over the photo montage, so no lips are affected.

## Reels pilot (source #2, the 59-second wolf and pig story)
- **Pilot video:** in `Downloads\Telugu_Reels_Project\03_Approved_Pilot\`, as `<source name>_TELUGU_FINAL.mp4` (attached).
- **SRT:** the same SRT is in `05_Subtitle_Files` and attached.
- **Project setup:** all 40 sources and 6 references are copied into the project folders, with a progress tracker in `07_Quality_Reports`. The originals are untouched.

**What's in it:**
- **Dialogue:** all 15 English lines are accounted for, with nothing added or dropped.
- **Voices:** the pig has its own worried voice, and the wolf reuses the Truth Machine father-wolf voice so the channel sounds consistent.
- **Captions:** the English captions are covered and Telugu subtitles sit in the same spot.
- **Mix:** the creator's original voice-forward balance is kept.

It passed the same QA as V3: Telugu on all 15 lines, no English left, 0 clipped samples, captions covered. The full report is in `pilot_02_quality_report.md`.

**Production preset:** `06_Working_Files\production_preset.json` holds the settings for the batch: voices, pace, 1.1× cap, subtitle style, mix and export. One rule changed during the pilot: music is only ever turned down, never up.

**Licensing, the one serious issue:** the 40 sources appear to be the Instagram account "quietwolfzz"'s posts, saved with download tools, and I found no permission with the files. Translating, re-voicing or covering the captions doesn't remove the creator's copyright in the story, art or music. Posting or monetizing them without written permission risks takedowns and strikes. I left the creator's watermark in place. The safe paths are written permission from the creator, or original Telugu reels built on the same idea with your own artwork.

**Timing for the batch:** the other 39 reels would take roughly 1–2 hours each on this PC.

import json, os, shutil, subprocess, sys
import numpy as np

# Stage A for one source: copy, audio, Demucs split, English transcript with words, caption strip
# location, per-phrase pitch (speaker hints) and a frame sheet at every phrase. usage: reel_prep.py src.mp4 workdir
src, wd = sys.argv[1:3]
PY = "C:/tgwork/venv/Scripts/python.exe"
os.makedirs(wd, exist_ok=True)
inp = os.path.join(wd, "input.mp4")
if not os.path.exists(inp): shutil.copy(src, inp)
run = lambda *a: subprocess.run(list(a), check=True)
probe = lambda e: subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "v:0", "-show_entries", e, "-of", "csv=p=0", inp],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
W, H = (int(v) for v in probe("stream=width,height").split(","))
if not os.path.exists(f"{wd}/audio.wav"):
    run("ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", inp, "-vn", "-ac", "2", "-ar", "44100", f"{wd}/audio.wav")
sep = f"{wd}/sep/htdemucs_ft/audio"
if not os.path.exists(f"{sep}/vocals.wav"):
    run(PY, "-m", "demucs", "--two-stems", "vocals", "-n", "htdemucs_ft", "-o", f"{wd}/sep", f"{wd}/audio.wav")
if not os.path.exists(f"{wd}/transcript.json"):
    run("ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", f"{sep}/vocals.wav", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000", f"{wd}/vocals16k.wav")
    run(PY, "C:/tgwork/scripts/transcribe.py", f"{wd}/vocals16k.wav", f"{wd}/transcript.json")

# caption strip: rows where bright text shows up in many frames (searched over the whole height)
raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", inp, "-vf", "fps=2,format=gray", "-f", "rawvideo", "-"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
v = np.frombuffer(raw, np.uint8); n = len(v) // (W * H); v = v[:n * W * H].reshape(n, H, W)
white = ((v[:, :, W // 7: W - W // 7] > 215).sum(2) > 6).mean(0)
k = np.convolve(white, np.ones(5) / 5, "same")
y = int(np.argmax(k[H // 8:])) + H // 8
lo, hi = y, y
while lo > 0 and k[lo - 1] > k[y] * 0.25: lo -= 1
while hi < H - 1 and k[hi + 1] > k[y] * 0.25: hi += 1
cap = {"W": W, "H": H, "y0": lo, "y1": hi, "peak_share": round(float(k[y]), 2)}

# per-phrase pitch + one frame per phrase so speakers can be identified
x = np.frombuffer(subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", f"{sep}/vocals.wav", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000", "-f", "f32le", "-"],
                                 capture_output=True, check=True).stdout, np.float32)
def f0(a, b):
    seg = x[int(a * 16000):int(b * 16000)]; m = 640; out = []
    if len(seg) < m * 2: return 0
    thr = np.percentile(np.abs(seg), 90) * 0.3
    for i in range(0, len(seg) - m, 320):
        f = seg[i:i + m] - seg[i:i + m].mean()
        if np.abs(f).max() < thr: continue
        ac = np.correlate(f, f, "full")[m - 1:]; kk = 40 + np.argmax(ac[40:228])
        if ac[kk] > 0.45 * ac[0]: out.append(16000 / kk)
    return int(np.median(out)) if out else 0
T = json.load(open(f"{wd}/transcript.json", encoding="utf-8"))
phrases, cur = [], []
for s in T:
    for w in s["words"]:
        cur.append(w)
        if w["w"].strip()[-1:] in ".?!,":
            phrases.append(cur); cur = []
    if cur: phrases.append(cur); cur = []
P = [{"s": p[0]["s"], "e": p[-1]["e"], "f0": f0(p[0]["s"], p[-1]["e"]), "text": "".join(w["w"] for w in p).strip()} for p in phrases]
os.makedirs(f"{wd}/frames", exist_ok=True)
for i, p in enumerate(P):
    run("ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-ss", f"{(p['s'] + p['e']) / 2:.2f}", "-i", inp, "-frames:v", "1", "-vf", "scale=240:-1", f"{wd}/frames/{i:03d}.png")
run("ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", f"{wd}/frames/%03d.png", "-vf", f"tile=8x{-(-len(P) // 8)}", "-frames:v", "1", f"{wd}/phrases_sheet.png")
json.dump({"caption": cap, "phrases": P, "duration": float(subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", inp], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)},
          open(f"{wd}/prep.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
print("prepped", wd, cap, len(P), "phrases")
EOF
cat > /c/tgwork/scripts/reel_prep_all.sh <<'EOF'

import json, os, shutil, subprocess, sys

src, wd = sys.argv[1:3]

os.makedirs(wd, exist_ok=True)
inp = os.path.join(wd, "input.mp4")
if not os.path.exists(inp): shutil.copy(src, inp)
run = lambda *a: subprocess.run(list(a), check=True)
probe = lambda e: subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "v:0", "-show_entries", e, "-of", "csv=p=0", inp],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
W, H = (int(v) for v in probe("stream=width,height").split(","))
if not os.path.exists(f"{wd}/audio.wav"):
    run("ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", inp, "-vn", "-ac", "2", "-ar", "44100", f"{wd}/audio.wav")
sep = f"{wd}/sep/htdemucs_ft/audio"
if not os.path.exists(f"{sep}/vocals.wav"):
    run(PY, "-m", "demucs", "--two-stems", "vocals", "-n", "htdemucs_ft", "-o", f"{wd}/sep", f"{wd}/audio.wav")
if not os.path.exists(f"{wd}/transcript.json"):
    run("ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", f"{sep}/vocals.wav", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000", f"{wd}/vocals16k.wav")
    run(PY, "C:/tgwork/scripts/transcribe.py", f"{wd}/vocals16k.wav", f"{wd}/transcript.json")

# caption strip: rows where bright text shows up in many frames (searched over the whole height)
raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", inp, "-vf", "fps=2,format=gray", "-f", "rawvideo", "-"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
v = np.frombuffer(raw, np.uint8); n = len(v) // (W * H); v = v[:n * W * H].reshape(n, H, W)
white = ((v[:, :, W // 7: W - W // 7] > 215).sum(2) > 6).mean(0)
k = np.convolve(white, np.ones(5) / 5, "same")
y = int(np.argmax(k[H // 8:])) + H // 8
lo, hi = y, y
while lo > 0 and k[lo - 1] > k[y] * 0.25: lo -= 1
while hi < H - 1 and k[hi + 1] > k[y] * 0.25: hi += 1
cap = {"W": W, "H": H, "y0": lo, "y1": hi, "peak_share": round(float(k[y]), 2)}

# per-phrase pitch + one frame per phrase so speakers can be identified
x = np.frombuffer(subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", f"{sep}/vocals.wav", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000", "-f", "f32le", "-"],

def f0(a, b):

    if len(seg) < m * 2: return 0
    thr = np.percentile(np.abs(seg), 90) * 0.3
    for i in range(0, len(seg) - m, 320):
        f = seg[i:i + m] - seg[i:i + m].mean()

        if ac[kk] > 0.45 * ac[0]: out.append(16000 / kk)
    return int(np.median(out)) if out else 0
T = json.load(open(f"{wd}/transcript.json", encoding="utf-8"))
phrases, cur = [], []
for s in T:
    for w in s["words"]:
        cur.append(w)
        if w["w"].strip()[-1:] in ".?!,":
            phrases.append(cur); cur = []
    if cur: phrases.append(cur); cur = []
P = [{"s": p[0]["s"], "e": p[-1]["e"], "f0": f0(p[0]["s"], p[-1]["e"]), "text": "".join(w["w"] for w in p).strip()} for p in phrases]

run("ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", f"{wd}/frames/%03d.png", "-vf", f"tile=8x{-(-len(P) // 8)}", "-frames:v", "1", f"{wd}/phrases_sheet.png")
json.dump({"caption": cap, "phrases": P, "duration": float(subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", inp], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)},
          open(f"{wd}/prep.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
print("prepped", wd, cap, len(P), "phrases")

import csv, glob, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys
import numpy as np

# Stage C for one reel, from its hand-written lines.json to a checked, delivered MP4:
# IndicF5 voices (1 take, then 2 more for any flagged line), take picking, assembly, subtitles,
# music bed, render, QA, delivery into the project folders and a tracker update.
# usage: reel_build.py N      (work dir C:/tgwork/reels/vNN, tracker row N)
N = int(sys.argv[1])
wd = f"C:/tgwork/reels/v{N:02d}"
R = "C:/Users/sowmy/Downloads/Telugu_Reels_Project"
PY, PY3 = "C:/tgwork/venv/Scripts/python.exe", "C:/tgwork/venv3/Scripts/python.exe"
S = "C:/tgwork/scripts"
env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8")
log = open(f"{wd}/build.log", "a", encoding="utf-8")

def run(*a, **kw):
    e = dict(env, **kw.pop("extra", {}))
    r = subprocess.run(list(a), capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", env=e)
    log.write(f"$ {' '.join(a)}\n{r.stdout}\n{r.stderr[-3000:]}\n"); log.flush()
    if r.returncode: raise SystemExit(f"step failed: {a[1] if len(a) > 1 else a[0]}")
    return r.stdout

prep = json.load(open(f"{wd}/prep.json", encoding="utf-8"))
cap, DUR = prep["caption"], prep["duration"]
W, H = cap["W"], cap["H"]
lines = json.load(open(f"{wd}/lines.json", encoding="utf-8"))
for i, ln in enumerate(lines):                       # time available to each line (same rule as assemble.py)
    prev_end = lines[i - 1]["end"] if i else 0
    start = max(ln["start"] - 0.25, prev_end + 0.08) if i else ln["start"]
    nxt = lines[i + 1]["start"] if i + 1 < len(lines) else DUR - 0.05
    ln["slot"] = round(nxt - 0.08 - start, 3)
json.dump(lines, open(f"{wd}/lines.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

# 1. voices: one paced take per line, then two more for every line the picker flags
gen = [PY3, f"{S}/f5_gen.py", f"{wd}/lines.json", f"{wd}/takes"]
run(*gen, "all", "C:/tgwork/reels/prompts.json", "1", extra={"PACE": "1", "TAG": "p"})
out = run(PY, f"{S}/pick_takes.py", f"{wd}/lines.json", f"{wd}/takes", f"{wd}/pick", extra={"DUR": str(DUR)})
flag = sorted({int(m.group(1)) for m in re.finditer(r"^(\d\d) \S+\s+pick \S+\s+read-back ([\d.]+)", out, re.M)
               if float(m.group(2)) < 0.55} | {int(l[:2]) for l in out.splitlines() if re.match(r"^\d\d ", l) and "BAD" in l.split("|")[0]})
# lines whose pick itself was BAD show "BAD" before the "|"? pick_takes marks only others; re-check picks:
flag = sorted(set(flag) | {i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if f"{i:02d} " in out and f"pick {i:02d}_p1.wav" in out and
                           re.search(rf"^{i:02d} .*?\(\d+, [\d.]+, '([^']+)'", out, re.M)})
if flag:
    run(*gen, ",".join(map(str, flag)), "C:/tgwork/reels/prompts.json", "2,3", extra={"PACE": "1", "TAG": "p"})
    out2 = run(PY, f"{S}/pick_takes.py", f"{wd}/lines.json", f"{wd}/takes", f"{wd}/pick",
               extra={"DUR": str(DUR), "ONLY": ",".join(map(str, flag))})
    out += "\n--- regenerated " + ",".join(map(str, flag)) + "\n" + out2
open(f"{wd}/pick_report.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(out)

# 2. text-free checks on the picks; smooth clicks
for f in glob.glob(f"{wd}/pick/*.wav"):
    run("ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", f, "-af", "adeclick", f[:-4] + "_d.wav")
    os.replace(f[:-4] + "_d.wav", f)
pros = run(PY, f"{S}/prosody.py", "clips", f"{wd}/pick")

# 3. assemble, background, subtitles, music bed, render
asm = run(PY, f"{S}/assemble.py", f"{wd}/lines.json", f"{wd}/pick", f"{wd}/sep/htdemucs_ft/audio/vocals.wav", str(DUR), wd,
          extra={"MAX_TEMPO": "1.1", "EARLY": "0.25"})
run(PY, f"{S}/background.py", f"{wd}/sep/htdemucs_ft/audio/no_vocals.wav", f"{wd}/sep/htdemucs_ft/audio/vocals.wav",
    f"{wd}/lines.json", f"{wd}/background.wav")
cy = (cap["y0"] + cap["y1"]) // 2
FS = round(54 * min(W, 0.75 * H) / 1000)
half = round(1.45 * FS)
y0, bh = max(0, cy - half), min(H - max(0, cy - half), 2 * half)
run(PY, f"{S}/reel_make_ass.py", f"{wd}/timed.json", "C:/tgwork/reels/preset.json", str(W), str(H), str(cy),
    f"{wd}/telugu.ass", f"{wd}/telugu.srt")
bed = run(PY, f"{S}/musicbed.py", f"{wd}/background.wav", f"{wd}/voice.wav", f"{wd}/background_bed.wav")
run(PY, f"{S}/reel_render.py", f"{wd}/input.mp4", f"{wd}/timed.json", f"{wd}/telugu.ass", f"{wd}/background_bed.wav",
    f"{wd}/voice.wav", f"{wd}/final.mp4", extra={"COVER": f"{y0},{bh}"})

# 4. QA
os.makedirs(f"{wd}/qa", exist_ok=True)
sw = 240 if W < H else 400
qa = run(PY, f"{S}/qa.py", f"{wd}/final.mp4", f"{wd}/timed.json", f"{wd}/transcript.json", f"{wd}/qa",
         extra={"CAPCROP": f"crop={W}:{bh + 16}:0:{max(0, y0 - 8)},scale={sw}:-1"})
raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", f"{wd}/final.mp4", "-f", "f32le", "-ac", "2", "-"], capture_output=True).stdout
st = np.frombuffer(raw, np.float32)
clipped, peak = int((np.abs(st) >= 0.999).sum()), float(np.abs(st).max())
bed_en = run(PY, "-c", "from faster_whisper import WhisperModel as M\n"
             f"s,_=M('medium.en',device='cpu',compute_type='int8').transcribe(r'{wd}/background_bed.wav',language='en',vad_filter=True)\n"
             "print('|'.join(x.text.strip() for x in s if x.no_speech_prob < 0.5 and x.avg_logprob > -0.7))").strip()
# caption samples where neither a Telugu subtitle nor the cover band would hide text: bright pixels in the strip
blank = []
for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"{wd}/qa/capstrip_*.png")):
    d = np.frombuffer(subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", f, "-vf", "format=gray", "-f", "rawvideo", "-"],
                                     capture_output=True).stdout, np.uint8)
    if (d > 200).sum() < 15: blank.append(os.path.basename(f))
langs = re.search(r"detected languages: (.*)", qa).group(1)

import csv, glob, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys
import numpy as np

# Stage C for one reel, from its hand-written lines.json to a checked, delivered MP4:
# IndicF5 voices (1 take, then 2 more for any flagged line), take picking, assembly, subtitles,
# music bed, render, QA, delivery into the project folders and a tracker update.
# usage: reel_build.py N      (work dir C:/tgwork/reels/vNN, tracker row N)
N = int(sys.argv[1])
wd = f"C:/tgwork/reels/v{N:02d}"
R = "C:/Users/sowmy/Downloads/Telugu_Reels_Project"
PY, PY3 = "C:/tgwork/venv/Scripts/python.exe", "C:/tgwork/venv3/Scripts/python.exe"
S = "C:/tgwork/scripts"
env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8")
log = open(f"{wd}/build.log", "a", encoding="utf-8")

def run(*a, **kw):
    e = dict(env, **kw.pop("extra", {}))
    r = subprocess.run(list(a), capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", env=e)
    log.write(f"$ {' '.join(a)}\n{r.stdout}\n{r.stderr[-3000:]}\n"); log.flush()
    if r.returncode: raise SystemExit(f"step failed: {a[1] if len(a) > 1 else a[0]}")
    return r.stdout

prep = json.load(open(f"{wd}/prep.json", encoding="utf-8"))
cap, DUR = prep["caption"], prep["duration"]
W, H = cap["W"], cap["H"]
lines = json.load(open(f"{wd}/lines.json", encoding="utf-8"))
for i, ln in enumerate(lines):                       # time available to each line (same rule as assemble.py)
    prev_end = lines[i - 1]["end"] if i else 0
    start = max(ln["start"] - 0.25, prev_end + 0.08) if i else ln["start"]
    nxt = lines[i + 1]["start"] if i + 1 < len(lines) else DUR - 0.05
    ln["slot"] = round(nxt - 0.08 - start, 3)
json.dump(lines, open(f"{wd}/lines.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

# 1. voices: one paced take per line, then two more for every line the picker flags
gen = [PY3, f"{S}/f5_gen.py", f"{wd}/lines.json", f"{wd}/takes"]
run(*gen, "all", "C:/tgwork/reels/prompts.json", "1", extra={"PACE": "1", "TAG": "p"})
out = run(PY, f"{S}/pick_takes.py", f"{wd}/lines.json", f"{wd}/takes", f"{wd}/pick", extra={"DUR": str(DUR)})
flag = sorted({int(m.group(1)) for m in re.finditer(r"^(\d\d) \S+\s+pick \S+\s+read-back ([\d.]+)", out, re.M)
               if float(m.group(2)) < 0.55} | {int(l[:2]) for l in out.splitlines() if re.match(r"^\d\d ", l) and "BAD" in l.split("|")[0]})
# lines whose pick itself was BAD show "BAD" before the "|"? pick_takes marks only others; re-check picks:
flag = sorted(set(flag) | {i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if f"{i:02d} " in out and f"pick {i:02d}_p1.wav" in out and
                           re.search(rf"^{i:02d} .*?\(\d+, [\d.]+, '([^']+)'", out, re.M)})
if flag:
    run(*gen, ",".join(map(str, flag)), "C:/tgwork/reels/prompts.json", "2,3", extra={"PACE": "1", "TAG": "p"})
    out2 = run(PY, f"{S}/pick_takes.py", f"{wd}/lines.json", f"{wd}/takes", f"{wd}/pick",
               extra={"DUR": str(DUR), "ONLY": ",".join(map(str, flag))})
    out += "\n--- regenerated " + ",".join(map(str, flag)) + "\n" + out2
open(f"{wd}/pick_report.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(out)

# 2. text-free checks on the picks; smooth clicks
for f in glob.glob(f"{wd}/pick/*.wav"):
    run("ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", f, "-af", "adeclick", f[:-4] + "_d.wav")
    os.replace(f[:-4] + "_d.wav", f)
pros = run(PY, f"{S}/prosody.py", "clips", f"{wd}/pick")

# 3. assemble, background, subtitles, music bed, render
asm = run(PY, f"{S}/assemble.py", f"{wd}/lines.json", f"{wd}/pick", f"{wd}/sep/htdemucs_ft/audio/vocals.wav", str(DUR), wd,
          extra={"MAX_TEMPO": "1.1", "EARLY": "0.25"})
run(PY, f"{S}/background.py", f"{wd}/sep/htdemucs_ft/audio/no_vocals.wav", f"{wd}/sep/htdemucs_ft/audio/vocals.wav",
    f"{wd}/lines.json", f"{wd}/background.wav")
cy = (cap["y0"] + cap["y1"]) // 2
FS = round(54 * min(W, 0.75 * H) / 1000)
half = round(1.45 * FS)
y0, bh = max(0, cy - half), min(H - max(0, cy - half), 2 * half)
run(PY, f"{S}/reel_make_ass.py", f"{wd}/timed.json", "C:/tgwork/reels/preset.json", str(W), str(H), str(cy),
    f"{wd}/telugu.ass", f"{wd}/telugu.srt")
bed = run(PY, f"{S}/musicbed.py", f"{wd}/background.wav", f"{wd}/voice.wav", f"{wd}/background_bed.wav")
run(PY, f"{S}/reel_render.py", f"{wd}/input.mp4", f"{wd}/timed.json", f"{wd}/telugu.ass", f"{wd}/background_bed.wav",
    f"{wd}/voice.wav", f"{wd}/final.mp4", extra={"COVER": f"{y0},{bh}"})

# 4. QA
os.makedirs(f"{wd}/qa", exist_ok=True)
sw = 240 if W < H else 400
qa = run(PY, f"{S}/qa.py", f"{wd}/final.mp4", f"{wd}/timed.json", f"{wd}/transcript.json", f"{wd}/qa",
         extra={"CAPCROP": f"crop={W}:{bh + 16}:0:{max(0, y0 - 8)},scale={sw}:-1"})
raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", f"{wd}/final.mp4", "-f", "f32le", "-ac", "2", "-"], capture_output=True).stdout
st = np.frombuffer(raw, np.float32)
clipped, peak = int((np.abs(st) >= 0.999).sum()), float(np.abs(st).max())
bed_en = run(PY, "-c", "from faster_whisper import WhisperModel as M\n"
             f"s,_=M('medium.en',device='cpu',compute_type='int8').transcribe(r'{wd}/background_bed.wav',language='en',vad_filter=True)\n"
             "print('|'.join(x.text.strip() for x in s if x.no_speech_prob < 0.5 and x.avg_logprob > -0.7))").strip()
# caption samples where neither a Telugu subtitle nor the cover band would hide text: bright pixels in the strip
blank = []
for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"{wd}/qa/capstrip_*.png")):
    d = np.frombuffer(subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", f, "-vf", "format=gray", "-f", "rawvideo", "-"],
                                     capture_output=True).stdout, np.uint8)
    if (d > 200).sum() < 15: blank.append(os.path.basename(f))
langs = re.search(r"detected languages: (.*)", qa).group(1)
loud = re.search(r"I:\s+(-?[\d.]+) LUFS.*?Peak:\s+(-?[\d.]+) dBFS", qa)
over = [l for l in asm.splitlines() if "OVERRUN" in l]
late = max(l["start"] - l["en_start"] for l in json.load(open(f"{wd}/timed.json", encoding="utf-8")))
spec = re.findall(r"codec_name=(\w+)\|profile=([\w ]+)\|(?:width=(\d+)\|height=(\d+))?", qa)
dur_out = float(re.search(r"format\|duration=([\d.]+)", qa).group(1))
problems = []
if clipped: problems.append(f"{clipped} clipped samples")
if bed_en: problems.append(f"possible English in music bed: {bed_en[:120]}")
if "'en'" in langs: problems.append("a line detected as English")
if dur_out < DUR - 0.2: problems.append("output shorter than source")
status = "Passed" if not problems else "CHECK: " + "; ".join(problems)
report = (f"# v{N:02d} QA\nsource duration {DUR:.1f}s -> output {dur_out:.1f}s, {W}x{H}\nstreams {spec}\n"
          f"loudness {loud.group(1) if loud else '?'} LUFS, true peak {loud.group(2) if loud else '?'} dBFS, stereo peak {peak:.3f}, clipped {clipped}\n"
          f"line languages {langs}\nEnglish in music bed: {bed_en or 'none'}\n"
          f"caption samples showing only the cover band: {len(blank)} {blank}\nlatest line start vs English: {late:+.2f}s\n"
          f"overruns (lines needing >1.1x, voice runs on): {over or 'none'}\nregenerated lines: {flag or 'none'}\n"
          f"music: {bed.strip()}\n\n## take picks\n{out}\n\n## delivery checks\n{pros}\n\n## qa.py\n{qa}\nSTATUS: {status}\n")
open(f"{wd}/qa_report.md", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(report)

# 5. deliver + tracker
rows = list(csv.reader(open(f"{R}/07_Quality_Reports/progress_tracker.csv", encoding="utf-8")))
row = next(r for r in rows if r[0] == str(N))
base = os.path.splitext(row[1])[0]
shutil.copy(f"{wd}/final.mp4", f"{R}/04_Final_Telugu_Videos/{base}_TELUGU_FINAL.mp4")
shutil.copy(f"{wd}/telugu.srt", f"{R}/05_Subtitle_Files/{base}_TELUGU.srt")
shutil.copy(f"{wd}/qa_report.md", f"{R}/07_Quality_Reports/{N:02d}_qa_report.md")
os.makedirs(f"{R}/06_Working_Files/v{N:02d}", exist_ok=True)
for f in ("lines.json", "timed.json", "telugu.ass", "transcript.json", "pick_report.txt"):
    shutil.copy(f"{wd}/{f}", f"{R}/06_Working_Files/v{N:02d}/{f}")
row[6:11] = ["Done", "Passed" if not (clipped or bed_en or "'en'" in langs) else "CHECK", "Passed", "Exported", status]
row[11] = "Third-party (quietwolfzz) - not cleared for publication; needs authorized or original visuals"
csv.writer(open(f"{R}/07_Quality_Reports/progress_tracker.csv", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="")).writerows(rows)
print(f"v{N:02d} {status}")

run(PY, f"{S}/reel_render.py", f"{wd}/input.mp4", f"{wd}/timed.json", f"{wd}/telugu.ass", f"{wd}/background_bed.wav",

             "print('|'.join(x.text.strip() for x in s if x.no_speech_prob < 0.5 and x.avg_logprob > -0.7))").strip()
# caption samples where neither a Telugu subtitle nor the cover band would hide text: bright pixels in the strip
blank = []
for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"{wd}/qa/capstrip_*.png")):
    d = np.frombuffer(subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", f, "-vf", "format=gray", "-f", "rawvideo", "-"],
                                     capture_output=True).stdout, np.uint8)
    if (d > 200).sum() < 15: blank.append(os.path.basename(f))
langs = re.search(r"detected languages: (.*)", qa).group(1)
loud = re.search(r"I:\s+(-?[\d.]+) LUFS.*?Peak:\s+(-?[\d.]+) dBFS", qa)
over = [l for l in asm.splitlines() if "OVERRUN" in l]
late = max(l["start"] - l["en_start"] for l in json.load(open(f"{wd}/timed.json", encoding="utf-8")))
spec = re.findall(r"codec_name=(\w+)\|profile=([\w ]+)\|(?:width=(\d+)\|height=(\d+))?", qa)
dur_out = float(re.search(r"format\|duration=([\d.]+)", qa).group(1))
problems = []
if clipped: problems.append(f"{clipped} clipped samples")

if "'en'" in langs: problems.append("a line detected as English")

import json, subprocess, sys

# Final render: cover band (whenever an English caption or Telugu subtitle is on screen),
# Telugu subtitles, background + Telugu voice mix. H.264/AAC MP4 at source resolution.
video, timed_json, ass, background, voice, out = sys.argv[1:7]
timed = json.load(open(timed_json, encoding="utf-8"))

windows = []
for ln in timed:
    windows.append((ln["en_start"] - 0.3, ln["en_end"] + 0.3))
    windows.append((ln["start"] - 0.1, ln["end"] + 0.3))
windows.sort()
merged = []
for a, b in windows:
    if merged and a <= merged[-1][1] + 0.4:
        merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], b)
    else:
        merged.append([max(0, a), b])
enable = "+".join(f"between(t,{a:.2f},{b:.2f})" for a, b in merged)

def probe(path):
    return float(subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "csv=p=0", path],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip())

# Hold the last frame (and pad the background) only if the Telugu voice outlasts the picture.
extra = max(0.0, probe(voice) - probe(video))
hold = f",tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration={extra:.2f}" if extra > 0.01 else ""
bgpad = f"apad=pad_dur={extra:.2f}," if extra > 0.01 else ""
print(f"holding last frame for {extra:.2f}s" if hold else "no frame hold needed")

# cover band geometry comes from the caption strip found for this video: COVER="y0,height"
import os
y0, bh = (int(v) for v in os.environ["COVER"].split(","))
w = int(subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "v:0", "-show_entries", "stream=width", "-of", "csv=p=0", video],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip())
template = (f"split[a][b];[b]crop={w}:{bh}:0:{y0},boxblur=16:3,colorlevels=romax=0.55:gomax=0.55:bomax=0.55,format=yuva420p,"
            f"geq=lum='p(X,Y)':cb='p(X,Y)':cr='p(X,Y)':a='255*min(1,min(Y,{bh - 1}-Y)/20)'[band];"
            f"[a][band]overlay=0:{y0}:enable='ENABLE',subtitles=SUBS:fontsdir=C\\\\:/Windows/Fonts")
vf = template.replace("ENABLE", enable).replace("SUBS", ass.replace("\\", "/").replace(":", "\\\\:"))
filt = (f"[0:v]{vf}{hold}[v];[1:a]{bgpad}anull[bg];"
        f"[bg][2:a]amix=inputs=2:duration=longest:normalize=0:weights='0.8 0.8',"
        f"loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1.5:LRA=11,aresample=44100[a]")
cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-stats", "-y", "-i", video, "-i", background, "-i", voice,
       "-filter_complex", filt, "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]",
       "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "slow", "-crf", "16", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-profile:v", "high",
       "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-ar", "44100", "-movflags", "+faststart", out]
print(len(merged), "cover windows")
subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

json.dump(P, open("C:/tgwork/reels/prompts.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1); print(len(x)/SR, "s prompt")
EOF
